FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 2) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft was finalized by the 
Weights and Measures Sectional Committee and approval of the Production and General Engineering Division 
Council. 


In the formulation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from standards of Weights and 
Measures (General) (Third Amendment) Rules, 1997 ‘Specification for Non- Automatic Weighing Instruments’. 


This standard supersedes the following Indian Standards: 


IS No. Title 


1435:1991 Platform weighing machines — Specification (first revision) 

1436: 1991 Weigh bridge — Specification ( first revision) 

1438: 1960 Specification for crane weighing machine 

1439: 1990 Steel yards — Specification ( first revision) 

1702 : 1967 Specification for spring balance (first revision) 

1853 : 1961 Specification for self-indicating and semi-self indicating counter type weighing machine 
1854: 1964 Specification for person weighing machine ( first revision) 

2489: 1963 Specification for baby weighing machine 

4070: 1967 Specification for wheel weighers 


This Indian Standard is published in two parts. The other part in this series is: 
Part 1 Terminology and definition 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final 
value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )’.

Indian Standard 


SPECIFICATION FOR NON-AUTOMATIC 
WEIGHING INSTRUMENTS 


PART 2 METROLOGICAL AND TECHNICAL 
REQUIREMENTS 


1 SCOPE 


This Indian Standard (Part 2) specifies the metrological 
and technical requirements for non-automatic weighing 
instruments and shall not be applicable to the following 
non-graduated instruments: 


a) Beam scale, and 
b) Counter machine. 


2 PRINCIPLES INVOLVED 


2.1 Units of Measurement 


The units of mass to be used on an instrument shall be 
the kilogram (kg), the milligram (mg), the gram (g) and 
tonne (t). 


2.1.2 For special application, for example, trade with 
precious stones, the metric carat (1 carat = 0.2 g) may 
be used as unit of measurement. The symbol for the 
carat shall be ‘c’. 
2.2 Metrological Requirements 
These requirements apply to all instruments irrespective 
of their principles of measurement. 
2.2.1 The instruments are classified according to: 

a) The verification scale interval; and 

b) The number of verification scale intervals. 
2.2.2 The maximum permissible errors shall be in 


the order of magnitude of the verification scale 
interval. 


2.2.3 A minimum capacity (Min) shall be specified 
to indicate that the instrument shall not be used for 
measuring loads below that limit. 


3 METROLOGICAL REQUIREMENTS

3.1.1 Accuracy Classes 


The accuracy classes for instrument and their symbols 
shall be as given in Table 1.

classes I and II or in classes II and III. The instrument 
as a whole shall then comply with the more severe 
requirements given at 3.9 applicable to either of the 
two classes.

The number of verification scale intervals n for each

3.4.4 Instrument with a Tare Device 


The requirements concerning the range of a multi- 
interval instrument apply to the net load for every 
possible value of the tare.

3.5.4 Minimum Capacity 


The minimum capacity of the instrument shall be 
determined in conformity with the requirements given 
in Table 3. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


3.5.5 Minimum Number of Verification Scale Intervals 


For an instrument of class I with d < 0.1 mg, n may be 
less than 50 000. 


3.6 Maximum Permissible Errors 


3.6.1 Values of Maximum Permissible Errors on 
Verification/Re- Verification 


The maximum permissible errors allowed for increasing 
or decreasing loads shall be as given in Table 5. 


3.6.2 Values of Maximum Permissible Errors in 
Inspection 


The maximum permissible errors during inspection 
shall be twice the maximum permissible errors allowed 
on verification. 


3.6.3 Basic Rules Concerning the Determination of 
Errors 


3.6.3.1 Influence factors 


The errors shall be determined under normal test 
condition, when the effect of one factor is being 
evaluated; all other factors shall be kept relatively 
constant, at a value close to normal. 


3.6.3.2 Maximum permissible errors for net values 


The maximum permissible errors apply to the net value 
of the load for every possible tare load, except preset 
tare values. 


3.6.3.3 Tare weighing device 


The maximum permissible error for a tare-weighing 
device shall be the same, for any tare value as those of 
the instrument, for the same value of load. 


3.7 Permissible Difference Between Results 


The error of any single weighing result by itself shall 
not exceed the maximum permissible error for the 
given load irrespective of what variation of results is 
permitted. 


3.7.1 Repeatability 


The difference between the maximum and minimum 
results of several weighings of the same load shall not 


Table 5 Maximum Permissible Errors Allowed 
( Clause 3.6.1 )

be greater than the absolute value of the maximum 
permissible error for the given load. 


3.7.2 Eccentric Loading 


The indications for different positions of a load 
shall meet the maximum permissible errors, when 
the instrument is tested in accordance with 3.7.2.1 
to 3.7.2.4. 


3.7.21 Unless otherwise specified hereafter, a load 
corresponding to one third (1/3) of the sum of the 
maximum capacity and the corresponding maximum 
additive tare effect shall be applied. 


3.7.2.2 On an instrument with a load receptor having 
n points of support, with n > 4, the fraction 1/(n -1) of 
the sum of the maximum capacity and the maximum 
additive tare effect shall be applied to each point of 
support. 


3.7.2.3 On an instrument with a load receptor subject to 
minimal off-center loading (for example, tank, hopper 
etc.) a test load corresponding to one-tenth (1/10) of 
the sum of the maximum capacity and the maximum 
additive tare effect shall be applied to each point of 
support. 


3.7.2.4 On an instrument used for weighing rolling loads 
(for example, vehicle scale, rail suspension instrument) 
a rolling test load corresponding to the usual rolling 
load, the heaviest and the most concentrate one which 
may be weighed, but not exceeding 0.8 times the sum 
of the maximum capacity and the maximum additive 
tare effect, shall be applied at different points on the 
load receptor. 


3.7.3 Multiple Indicating Device 


For a given load the difference between the indications 
of multiple indicating devices including tare weighing 
device, shall be not greater than the absolute value 
of the maximum permissible error, but shall be zero 
between digital indicating and printing devices. 


3.7.4 Different Positions of Equilibrium 


The difference between two results obtained for the 
same load when the method of balancing the load is 
changed (in the case of an instrument fitted with a 
device for extending the self-indication capacity) in 
two consecutive tests, shall not exceed the absolute 
value of the maximum permissible error for the applied 
load. 


3.8 Discrimination 
3.8.1 Non-self-Indicating Instrument 


An extra load equivalent to the value of the maximum 
permissible error for the applied load when gently 
placed or withdrawn from the instrument at equilibrium 
shall produce movement as required at 6.1. 


3.8.2 Self or Semi-self Indicating Instrument 
3.8.2.1 Analogue indication 


An extra load equivalent to the maximum permissible 
error for applied load when placed gently on or 
withdrawn from the instrument at equilibrium shall 
cause a permanent displacement of the indicating 
element corresponding to not less than 0.7 times the 
extra load. 


3.8.2.2 Digital indication 


An additional load equal to 1.4 times the actual scale 
interval, when gently placed on or withdrawn from 
the instrument at equilibrium shall change the initial 
indication. 


3.9 Variation due to Influence of Quantities and 
Time 


An instrument shall comply, unless otherwise specified 
at 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8, under the conditions given at 3.9.2 
and 3.9.3 and additionally it shall comply with the 
requirements given at 3.9.1, 3.9.2, 3.9.3 and 3.9.4. 


3.9.1 Tilting 


3.9.1.1 For instrument of class II, III or IV liable to be 
tilted, the influence of tilting shall be determined under 
the effect of a lengthwise or transverse tilting equal 
to 2/1 000 or corresponding to the limiting value of 
tilting marked on, or indicated by a level indicator, 
whichever is the greater tilt. 


The absolute value of the difference between the 
indication of the instrument in its reference position 
(not tilted) and the indication in the tilted position shall 
not exceed: 


a) At no load, two verification scale intervals, (the 
instrument having first been adjusted to zero at no 
load in its reference position) except instruments 
of class I. 


b) At self-indication capacity and at maximum 
capacity, the maximum permissible error (the 
instrument having been adjusted to zero at no load 
both in the reference and in the tilted position). 


An instrument shall be fitted with a leveling 

device and a lever indicator fixed firmly on the 

instrument in a place clearly visible to the user, 

unless the instrument is: 

1) Freely suspended, 

2) Installed in a fixed position or on tilting 
when; and 

3) Complying with the requirements on tilting 
when tilted to 5 percent in any direction. 

c 


Nas 


The limiting value of the level indicator shall be 
obvious, so that tilting is easily noticed. 


NOTE — Limiting value of tilting: Displacement of 2 mm 
from a central position 


3.9.1.2 On a class I instrument, the limiting value 
of tilting shall correspond to a tilt of not more than 
2/1000 otherwise, the instrument shall meet the 
requirements for instruments of class II. 


3.9.2 Temperature 


3.9.2.1 Prescribed temperature limits 


If no particular working temperature is stated in 
the descriptive markings of an instrument, then this 
instrument shall maintain its metrological properties 
within the temperature limits of -10°C and + 40°C 


3.9.2.2 Special temperature limits 


a) An instrument for which particular limits of 
working temperature are stated in the descriptive 
markings shall comply with the metrological 
requirements within those limits. 


b) The limits may be chosen according to the 
application of the instrument. 
c) The ranges within those limits shall be at least 


equal to: 

1) 5°C for instruments of class (1); 

2) 15°C for instruments of class (II); and 

3) 30°C for instruments of class (IID) and (IV). 


3.9.2.3 Temperature effect on no-load indication 


a) The indication at zero or near zero shall not vary 
by more than one verification scale interval for 
a difference in ambient temperature of 1°C for 
instruments of class I and 5°C for other classes. 


b) For multi-interval instruments and for multiple 
range instruments this applies to the smallest 
verification scale interval of the instrument. 


3.9.3 Main Power Supply 


An instrument operated from a main power supply 
shall comply with the metrological requirements if the 
power supply varies 


a) In voltage from - 15 percent to + 10 percent of the 
value marked on the instrument. 


b) In frequency from -2 percent to +2 percent of 
the value marked on the instrument, if alternate 
current is used. 


3.9.4 Time 


Under reasonable constant environmental conditions, 
an instrument of class I, Il, III or IV shall meet the 
following requirements. 


3.9.4.1 When load is kept on the instrument, the 
difference between the indication obtained immediately 
after placing a load and the indication observed during 
the following 30 min, shall not exceed 0.5e. However, 
the difference between the indications obtained at 
15 min and after that at 30 min shall not exceed 0.2e. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


If these conditions are not met, the difference between 
the indication obtained immediately after placing a 
load on the instrument and the indication observed 
during the following four hours shall not exceed the 
absolute value of the maximum permissible error at the 
load applied. 


3.9.4.2 The deviation shall not exceed 0.5e, on returning 
to zero as soon as the indication has been stabilized after 
the removal of any load, which has remained on the 
instrument for one and half hour. For a multi-interval 
instrument, the deviation shall not exceed 0.5e. 


On a multiple range instrument, the deviation shall 
not exceed 0.5e, on returning to zero from Max, 
Furthermore, after returning to zero from any load 
greater than Max, and immediately after switching to 
the lowest weighing range, the indication near zero 
shall not vary by more than e, during the following 
5 min. 


3.9.4.3 The durability error due to wear and tear 
shall not be greater than the value of the maximum 
permissible error. 

Adherence to this requirement is assumed if the 
instrument has passed the endurance test specified 


at 9, which shall be performed only for instruments 
with Max < 100 kg. 


3.10 Pattern Evaluation Tests 


Upon pattern evaluation, the tests given at 9 and 
Annex A shall be performed, to verify adherence to 
the requirements given at 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 and 3.9.1 to 
3.9.4, 4.5, 4.6, 5.3 and 6.1. The endurance test shall be 
performed after all other test given at 9 and Annex A. 


4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS FORA SELF 
OR SEMI-SELF INDICATING INSTRUMENTS 


4.1 General Requirements of Construction 
4.1.1 Suitability 


4.1.1.1 Suitability for application 


An instrument shall be designed to suit its intended 
purpose of use. 


4.1.1.2 Suitability for use 


An instrument shall be solidly and carefully constructed 
in order to ensure that it maintains its metrological 
qualities during a period of use. 


4.1.1.3 Suitability for verification 


a) An instrument shall permit the tests set out in this 
specification to perform. 


b) In particular, load receptors shall be such that the 
standard masses can be deposited on them easily 
and in total safety. If weights cannot be placed, an 
additional support may be required. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


c) It must be possible to identify devices that have 
been subject to a separate type examination 
procedure (such as load cells, printers etc.) 


4.1.2 Security 
4.1.2.1 Fraudulent use 


An instrument shall have no characteristics likely to 
facilitate its fraudulent use. 


4.1.2.2 Accidental breakdown and maladjustment 


An instrument shall be so constructed that an accidental 
breakdown or maladjustment of control elements likely 
to disturb its correct functioning cannot take place 
without its effect being evident. 


4.1.2.3 Controls 


Controls shall be so designed that they cannot normally 
come to rest in positions other than those intended by 
design, unless during the maneuver all indication is 
made possible, keys shall be marked unambiguously. 


4.1.2.4 Securing (sealing) of components and pre-set 
controls 


a) An instrument shall have provisions as required by 
the Department of Legal Metrology, for securing 
components and pre-set controls to which access 
or adjustment likely to affect the metrological 
characteristics of the instrument, is possible. 


b) Ona class I instrument devices to adjust sensitivity 
may remain unsecured. 


4.1.2.5 Adjustment 


If an instrument is fitted with an automatic or a semi- 
automatic span adjustment device, this device shall be 
incorporated inside the instrument. External influence 
upon this device shall be practically impossible after 
sealing. 


4.1.2.6 Gravity compensation 


A gravity sensitive instrument may be equipped with a 
device for compensating the effects of gravity variation. 
After securing, external influence on or access to this 
device shall be practically impossible. 


4.2 Indication of Weighing Results 

4.2.1 Quality of Reading 

4.2.1.1 Reading of the results shall be reliable, easy and 
unambiguous under conditions of normal use: 


a) The overall inaccuracy of reading of an analogue 
indicating device shall not exceed 0.2e. 


b) The figures forming the results shall be of a size, 
shape and clarity for reading to be easy. 


4.2.1.2 The scale, numbering and printing shall permit 
the figures, which form the results to be read by simple 
juxtaposition. Provided that this requirement shall not 


be applicable in the case of steel yard type weighing 
instruments. 


4.2.2 Form of the Indication 


4.2.2.1 Weighing results shall contain the names 
or symbols of the units of mass in which they are 
expressed. For any one indication of weight, only one 
unit of mass shall be used. The scale interval shall be in 
the form 1 x 1042 x 10*, or 5 x 10k, in which the result 
is expressed, the index k being a positive or negative 
whole number or equal to zero. All indicating, printing 
and tare weighing devices of an instrument shall be 
within any one weighing range, have the same scale 
interval for any given load. 


4.2.2.2 A digital indication shall display at least one 
figure beginning at the extreme right. Where the scale 
interval is changed automatically, the decimal sign 
shall maintain its position in the display. 


4.2.2.3 A decimal fraction shall be separated from its 
integer by a decimal sign (comma or dot), with the 
indication showing at least one figure to the left of the 
sign and all figures to the right. Zero may be indicated 
by one zero to the extreme right, without a decimal sign. 


4.2.2.4 The unit of mass shall be chosen so that weight 
values have not more than one non-significant zero 
to the right. For values with decimal sign, the non- 
significant zero is allowed only in the third position 
after the decimal sign. 


4.2.3 Limits of Indication 


There shall be no indication above Max + 9e. 


4.2.4 Approximate Indication Device 


The scale interval of an approximate indicating device 
shall be greater than Max/100 without being smaller 
than 20e. This approximate device is considered, as 
giving secondary indications. 


4.2.5 Extending the Range of Self-Indication on a 
Semi-Self-Indicating Instrument 


The extension interval of the range of self-indication 
shall not be greater than the value of the self-indication 


capacity. 


4.2.5.1 The scale interval of extension of the range 
of the self-indication shall be equal to the capacity of 
self-indication (comparator instruments are excluded 
from the provision). 


4.2.5.2 An extension device with accessible sliding 
poises is subject to the requirements specified at 6.2.2. 


4.2.5.3 On an extension device with enclosed sliding 
poises or mass switching mechanisms each extension 
should involve an adequate change in the numbering. It 
shall be possible to seal the housing and the adjusting 
cavities of the weights or masses. 


4.3 Analogue Indicating Device 


The following requirements apply in addition to those 
given at 4.2.1, 4.2.2, 4.2.3 and 4.2.4. 


4.3.1 Scale Marks (Length and Width) 


Scale shall be designed and numbered so that reading 
the weighing results is easy and unambiguous. 


4.3.1.1 Forms of scale marks 


Scale marks shall consist of lines of equal thickness: 
this thickness shall be constant and between 1/10 
and 1/4 of the scale spacing, without being less than 
0.2 mm. The length of the shortest scale mark shall be 
at least equal to the scale spacing. 


4.3.1.2 Arrangements of scale marks 


Scale marks shall be arranged in accordance with one 
of the sketches as shown in Fig. 3 (the line joining the 
end of the scale marks optional). 


2.40" 


tii 


5.10" 


ili tial 


Fic. 3 EXAMPLE OF THE APPLICATION TO 
RECTILINEAR SCALE 


4.3.1.3 Numbering 


a) On one scale, the scale interval of numbering 
shall be constant, in the form 1 x 10*, 2 x 105, 
5 x 10* units (k being a positive or a negative 
whole number or equal to zero), not greater than 
25 times the scale interval of the instrument. 


b 


wm 


If the scale is projected on a screen, at least two 
numbered scale marks shall appear wholly in the 
projected zone. 


c 


wa 


The height of the number (real or apparent) 
expressed in millimeters shall be not less than 3 
times the minimum reading distance expressed in 
meters, without being less than 2 mm. This height 
shall be proportional to the length of the scale 
mark to which it relates. 


d 


wm 


The width of a number, measured parallel to the 
base of the scale, shall be less than the distance 
between two consecutive numbered scale marks. 


4.3.1.4 Indicating component 


a) The width of the pointer of the indicating 
components shall be approximately equal to that 
of the scale marks and of a length such that the tip 
is at least level with the shortest mark. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


b) The distance between the scale and the pointer 
shall be at the most equal to the scale spacing, 
without being greater than 2 mm. 


4.3.2 Scale Spacing 


4.3.2.1 The scale spacing on an instrument of class I or 
II shall be: 


a) 1 mm for indicating devices; and 


b) 0.25 mm for complementary indicating devices; 


4.3.2.2 The scale spacing on an instrument of class ITI 
and IV shall be: 


a) 1.25 mm for dial indicating devices; and 
b) 1.75 mm for optical projection indicating devices. 


4.3.3 Limits of Indication 


4.3.3.1 Stops shall be provided to limit the movement 
of the indicating component whilst allowing it to travel 
below zero and above the capacity of self-indication. 
This requirement does not apply to multi-revolution 
dial instruments. 


4.3.3.2 The stops limiting the movement of the 
indicating components shall permit it to travel across 
zones of at least 4 scales spacing below zero and above 
the capacity of self-indication (three zones are not 
provided with a scale on fan charts and on dials with a 
single revolution pointer they are called ‘blank zone’). 


4.3.4 Damping 


4.3.4.1 Damping shall achieve a stable indication 
within 5 simple half periods of oscillation. 


4.3.4.2 Hydraulic damping elements sensitive to 
variations in temperature shall be provided with an 
automotive regulating device or an easily accessibly 
manual regulating device. It shall be impossible for 
the fluid of hydraulic damping elements on portable 
instruments to spill when the instruments in inclined 
at 45°. 


4.4 Digital Indicating and Printing Devices 

The following requirements apply in addition to those 
given at 4.2.1 to 4.2.5. 

4.4.1 Change of Indication 

After a change in load, the previous indication shall not 
persist for longer than 1 s. 

4.4.2 Stable Equilibrium 

The equilibrium is deemed stable when: 


a) In case of printing and/or data storage, the 
requirements given at 4.4.5.4 are met; and 

b) Incase of zero or tare operations (see 4.5.4, 4.5.6, 
4.5.7 and 4.6.8) it is sufficiently close to the final 
equilibrium to allow a correct operation of the 
device within relevant accuracy requirements. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


4.4.3 Extended Indicating Device 


4.4.3.1 An extended indicating device shall not be used 
on an instrument with a differentiated scale division. 


4.4.3.2 When an instrument is fitted with an extended 
indicating device, displaying the indication with a scale 
interval smaller than “e' shall be possible only: 


a) During pressing a key, or 


b) For a period not exceeding 5 s after a manual 
command in any case printing shall not be possible. 


4.4.4 Multiple Use of Indicating Device 


4.4.4.1 Indications other than primary indication may 
be displayed in the same indicating device, provided 
that: 


a) Quantities other than weight values are identified 
by the appropriate unit of measurement, or symbol 
thereof, or a special sign. 


b) Weight values that are not weighing results 
(see 5.2.1 to 5.2.3) shall be clearly identified, or 
they may be displayed only temporarily on manual 
command and shall not be printed. 


4.4.4.2 No restrictions apply if the weighing mode is 
made inoperative by a special command. 


4.4.5 Printing Device 


4.4.5.1 Printing shall be clear and permanent for the 
intended use, printed figures shall be at least 2 mm high. 


4.4.5.2 If printing takes place, the name or the symbol 
of the unit of measurement shall be either to the right of 
the value or above a column of values. 


4.4.5.3 Printing shall be 
equilibrium is not stable. 


impossible when the 


4.4.5.4 Stable equilibrium is considered to be achieved 
when over a period of 5 s following printout, no more 
than two adjacent values are indicated, one of which 
being the printed value. 


4.4.6 Memory Storage Device 


The storage of primary indications for subsequent 
indication, date transfer, totalizing, etc., shall be 
impossible when the equilibrium is not stable, the 
criterion of stable equilibrium is the same as specified 
at 4.5. 


4.5 Zero Setting and Zero-Tracking Devices 


An instrument may have one or more zero-setting 
devices and shall have not more than one zero tracking 
devices. 


4.5.1 Maximum Effect 


4.5.1.1 The effect of any zero-setting device shall 
not alter the maximum weighing capacity of the 
instrument. 


4.5.1.2 The overall effect of zero-setting and zero- 
tracking device shall not be more than 4 percent and of 
the initial zero-setting device not more than 20 percent 
of the maximum capacity. 


4.5.2 Accuracy 


After zero setting, the effect of zero deviation on the 
result of the weighing shall not be more than 0.25e, 
however, on an instrument with auxiliary indicating 
device this effect shall not be more than 0.5d. 


4.5.3 Multiple Range Instrument 


Zero setting in any weighing range shall be effective 
also in the greater weighing ranges if switching to a 
greater weighing range is possible while the instrument 
is loaded. 


4.5.4 Control of the Zero Setting Device 


4.5.4.1 An instrument except an instrument specified 
at 4.13 and 4.14, whether or not equipped with an 
initial zero-setting device may have a combined semi- 
automatic zero setting device and a semi-automatic 
tare-balancing device operated by the same key. 


4.5.4.2 If an instrument has a zero device and a tare- 
weighing device, the control of the zero-setting device 
shall be separate from that of the tare-weighing device. 


4.5.4.3 A semi-automatic zero setting device shall 
function only: 


a) When the instrument is in stable equilibrium; and 
b) It cancels any previous tare operation. 


4.5.5 Zero Indicating Devices on an Instrument with 
Digital Indication 


4.5.5.1 An instrument with digital indication shall 
have device that displays a special signal when the 
deviation from zero is not more than 0.25e. This device 
may also work when zero is indicated after a tare 
operation. 


4.5.5.2 This device is not mandatory on an instrument 
that has an auxiliary indicating or a zero-tracking device 
if the rate of zero tracking is not less than 0.25 d/s. 


4.5.6 Automatic Zero Setting Device 


An automatic zero-setting device shall operate only 
when the equilibrium is stable, and the indication has 
remained stable below zero as least 5 s. 


4.5.7 Zero-Tracking Device 


4.5.7.1 A zero tracking device shall operate only when: 


a) The indication is at zero, or at a negative net value 
equivalent to gross zero, 


b) The equilibrium is stable, and 
c) The corrections are not more than 0.5d/s. 
4.5.7.2 When zero is indicated after a tare operation, 


the zero tracking devices may operate within a range 
of 4 percent of maximum around the actual zero value. 


4.6 Tare Device 


4.6.1 General Requirements 


A tare device shall comply with the relevant provisions 
given at 4.1 to 4.4. 


4.6.2 Scale Interval 


The scale interval of a tare-weighing device shall be 
equal to the scale interval of the instrument for any 
given load. 


4.6.3 Accuracy 


4.6.3.1 A tare device shall permit setting the indication 
to zero with accuracy better than: 


a) + 0.25e for electronic instruments and any 
instrument with analogue indication; 

b) + 0.25e for mechanical instruments with digital 
indication and instruments with auxiliary 
indication device; and 


c) + 0.5e for mechanical instruments with digital 
indication and instruments with auxiliary 
indicating devices. 


4.6.3.2 On a multi-interval instrument e shall be 
replaced by e, 


4.6.4 Operating Range 


The tare device shall be such that it cannot be used at 
or below its zero effect or above its maximum indicated 
effect. 


4.6.5 Visibility of Operation 


4.6.5.1 Operation of the tare device shall be visibly 

indicated on the instrument. In the case of instruments 

with digital indication, this shall be done by marking 

the indicated net value with the sign ‘NET’ or “net”. 
NOTE — If an instrument is equipped with a device that 
allows the gross values to be displayed temporarily while a 
tare device is in operation, the ‘NET’ symbol disappear while 
the gross value is displayed. 


4.6.5.2 This is not required for an instrument with a 
combined semi-automatic zero-setting device and a 
semi-automatic tare-balancing device operated by the 
same key. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


4.6.6 Subtractive Tare Device 


When the use of subtractive tare device does not allow 
the value of the residual weighing range to be known, 
a device shall prevent the use of the instrument above 
its maximum capacity or indicate that this capacity has 
been reached. 


4.6.7 Multiple Range Instrument 


On a multiple range instrument the tare operation shall 
be effective also in the greater weighing ranges, if 
switching to a greater weighing range is possible while 
the instrument is loaded. 


4.6.8 Semi-Automatic or Automatic Tare Devices 


These devices shall operate only when the instrument is 
in stable equilibrium. 


4.6.9 Combined Zero-Setting and Tare Balancing Device 


If the semi-automatic zero setting device and semi- 
automatic tare-balancing device are operated by the 
same key (see 4.5.2 and 4.5.5) and if appropriate clause 
4.5.7 apply at any load. 


4.6.10 Consecutive Tare Operations 
4.6.10.1 Repeat operation of a tare device is permitted. 


4.6.10.2 If more than one tare device is operative at 
the same time, tare weight values shall be clearly 
designated when indicated or printed. 


4.6.11 Printing of Weighing Results 


4.6.11.1 Gross weight values may be printed without 
any designation. For a designation by a symbol, only 
‘G’ is permitted. 


4.6.11.2 If only net weight values are printed without 
corresponding gross or tare values, they may be printed 
without any designation. A symbol for designation shall 
be ‘N’. This applies also where semi-automatic zero 
setting and semi-automatic tare balancing are initiated 
by the same key. 


4.6.11.3 Gross, net or tare values determined by 
a multiple range instrument or by a multi-interval 
instrument need not be marked by a special designation 
referring to the (partial) weighing range. 


4.6.11.4 If net weight valves are printed together 
with the corresponding gross and/or tare values; the 
net and tare values shall at least be identified by the 
corresponding symbol ‘N’ and ‘T’. 


4.6.11.5 However, it is permitted to replace the symbols 
G, N, T by complete words. 


4.6.11.6 If net weight values and tare values determined 
by different tare devices are printed separately, they 
shall be suitable identified. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


4.7 Preset Tare Device 
4.7.1 Scale Interval 


Regardless of how a preset tare value is introduced 
into the device, its scale interval shall be equal or 
automatically rounded to the scale interval of the 
instrument. On a multiple range instrument, a preset 
tare value may only be transferred from one weighing 
range to another one with a larger verification scale 
interval but shall than be rounded to the later. For a 
multiple interval instrument, the maximum preset tare 
value shall not be greater than Max, and the indicated 
or printed, calculated net value shall be rounded to the 
scale interval of the instrument for the same net weight 
value. 


4.7.2 Modes of Operation 


4.7.2.1 A preset tare device may be operated together 
with one or more tare device provided that: 


a) Clause 4.6.10 is complied, and 


b) A preset tare operation cannot be modified or 
canceled as long as any tare device operated after 
the preset tare operation is still in use. 


4.7.2.2 Preset tare devices may operate automatically 
only if the preset tare value is clearly identified with the 
load to the measured. 


4.7.3 Indication of Operation 


4.7.3.1 For the indicating device clause 4.4.5 shall 
apply. It shall be possible to indicate the preset tare 
value at least temporarily 


4.7.3.2 Clause 4.6.9 applies accordingly provided, if 
the calculated net value is printed, at least the preset 
tare value is printed as well, with the exception of an 
instrument covered by 4.13, 4.14, or 4.16. Preset tare 
values are designated by the symbol ‘PT’ however; it 
is permitted to replace the symbol ‘PT’ by complete 
words. 


4.8 Locking Positions 


4.8.1 Prevention of Weighing Outside the ‘Weigh’ 
Position 


4.8.1.1 Ifan instrument has one or more locking device, 
these devices shall only have two stable positions 
corresponding to ‘locked’ and ‘weigh’ and weighing 
shall only be possible in the ‘weigh’ positions. 


4.8.12 A ‘pre-weigh’ position may exist on 
any instrument of class I or II except mentioned 
under 4.13, 4.15 or 4.16. 


4.8.2 Indication of Position 


The ‘locked’ and ‘weigh’ positions shall be clearly 
shown. 


10 


4.9 Auxiliary Calibration Devices (Removable or 
Fixed) 


4.9.1 Devices with One or More Platform 


a) The nominal value of the ratio between the 
weights to be placed on the platform to balance 
a certain load and this load shall not be less than 
1/5 000 (it shall be visibly indicated just above the 
platform). 


b 


eS 


The value of the weights needed to balance a load 
equal to the verification scale interval shall be an 
integer multiple of 0.1 g 


4.9.2 Numbered Scale Devices 


The scale interval of the auxiliary verification devices 
shall be equal to or smaller than 1/5 of the verification 
scale interval for which it is intended. 


4.10 Selection of Weighing Ranges on a Weighing 
Scale on a Multiple Range Instrument 


The range, which is actually in operation, shall be 
clearly indicated. 


4.10.1 Manual Selection of the Weighing Range is 
Allowed 


a) From a smaller to a greater weighing range at 
any load. 


b) From a greater to a smaller weighing range 
when there is no load on the load receptor and 
the indication is zero at a negative net value. 
The tare operation receptor shall be canceled 
and the zero shall be set to +0.25e both 
automatically. 


4.11 Device for Selection (or Switching) between 
Various Load Receptors — Load Transmitting 
Devices and Various Load Measuring Devices 


4.11.1 Compensation of No-Load Effect 


The selection device shall ensure compensation for the 
unequal no load effect of the various load receptors- 
load transmitting devices, in use. 


4.11.2 Zero Setting 


Zero setting of an instrument with any multiple 
combination of various load measuring devices and 
various load receptors shall be possible without any 
ambiguity and in accordance with the provisions 
specified at 4.5. 


4.11.3 Impossibility of Weighing 

Weighing shall not be possible while selection devices 
are being used. 

4.11.4 Identification of the Combination Use 


Combination of load receptors and measuring devices 
used shall be readily identifiable. 


4.12 ‘Plus’ and ‘Minus’ Comparative Instrument 


For the purpose of verification a ‘heavy’ or ‘plus’ and 
‘light’ or minus’ comparators instrument is considered 
to be a semi-self indicating instrument. 


4.12.1 Distinction Between ‘Plus’ and ‘Minus’ Zone 


a) On an analogue indicating devices, the ones 
situated on either side of zero shall be distinguished 
by ‘+’ and ‘-’. 

b) On a digital indicating device, an inscription 
nearer the indicating device shall be given: 

icici g (kg, t); and 


g (kg, t). 


1) Range + 
2) Range - 


4.12.2 Form of Scale 


Scale of a comparator instrument shall have at least one 
scale division d equal to e (d = e) on either of zero. The 
corresponding value shall be shown on either end of 
the scale. 


4.13 Additional Requirement for an Instrument for 
Direct Sales to the Public 


The following requirements apply to an instrument of 
class II, HI or IV with a maximum capacity not more 
than 100 kg capacity designed for direct sale to the 
public. 


4.13.1 Primary Indication 

On an instrument for direct sale to the public, the 
primary indications are the weighing results and the 
information about the correct zero position, tare, and 
pre-set tare operation. 


4.13.2 Zero Setting Device 


An instrument for direct sale to the public shall not be 
fitted with a non-automatic zero setting device unless 
operated with tool. 


4.13.3 Tare Device 


A mechanical instrument with a weight receptor shall 
not be fitted with a tare device. An instrument shall not 
be fitted with a device, which can recall the gross value 
while a tare or pre-set tare device is in operation. 


4.13.3.1 Non automatic tare device 

A displacement of 5 mm of a point of the control shall 
be at the most equal to one verification scale interval. 
4.13.3.2 Semi-automatic tare device 


An instrument may be fitted with semi-automatic tare 
device if: 
a) The action of the tare device does not permit the 
reduction of the tare; and 


b) Their effect can only be canceled when there is no 
load on the load receptor. 


11 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


4.13.3.2.1 In addition, the instrument shall comply with 
at least one of the following requirements: 


a) The tare value is indicated permanently in a 
separate display; 


b) The tare value is indicated with a sign ‘-’ (minus), 
when there is no load on the load receptor; or 


c) The effect of the device is canceled automatically 
when the indication returns to zero when unloading 
the load receptor after the stable net weighing 
results greater than zero has been indicated. 


4.13.3.3 Automatic tare device 


An instrument shall not be fitted with an automatic tare 
device. 


4.13.4 Preset Tare Device 


a) A preset tare device may be provided if the preset 
tare value is indicated as a primary indication on a 
separate display that is clearly differentiated from 
the weight display (see 4.13.3.2). 


b) It shall not be possible to operate a pre-set tare 
device, if a tare device is in use. 


c) Where a pre-set tare is associated with a price look 
up (PLU); the preset tare value may be canceled at 
the same time, as the PLU is cancelled. 


4.13.5 Impossibility of Weighing 


It shall be impossible to weigh or to guide the indicating 
element during the normal locking operation or during 
the normal operation of adding or subtracting weights. 


4.13.6 Visibility 


a) All primary indications shall be displayed clearly 
and simultaneously to both the vendor and the 
customer. 


b) Ondigital devices that display primary indications, 
the numerical figures on either set shall be of the 
same dimension and at least 10 mm high, with a 
tolerance of 0.5 mm. 


c) On an instrument to be used with weights, it shall 
be possible to distinguish the value of the weights. 


4.13.7 An instrument shall not be fitted with any 
auxiliary indicating device or an extended indicating 
device. 


4.13.8 Instrument of Class IT 


An instrument of class Il shall comply with the 
requirements given at 3.9. 


4.13.9 Significant Fault 


When a significant fault has been detected, a visible or 
audible alarm shall be provided for the customer, and 
data transmission to any peripheral equipment shall be 
prevented. The alarm shall continue until such time as 
the user takes action or the cause dis-appears. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


4.13.10 Counting Ratio 


The counting ratio on a mechanical counting instrument 
shall be 1/10 or 1/100. 


4.14 Additional Requirements for an Instrument for 
Direct Sale to the Public with Price Indication 


The following requirements are to be applied in addition 
to requirements given at 4.13. 


4.14.1 Primary Indications 


On a price-indicating instrument, the supplementary 
primary indications are unit price and price to pay and 
if applicable, number, unit price and price to pay for 
non-weighed articles and price totals. Price charts, such 
as fan charts, are not subject to the requirements of this 
specification. 


4.14.2 Instrument with Price Scales 


a) For unit price and price-to-pay scales, clause 4.2 
and 4.3.1 to 4.3.3 apply accordingly. The decimal 
shall be indicated to two places. 


b 


wm 


Reading from price scales shall be so possible that 
the absolute value of the difference between the 
product of the indicated weight W and unit price 
U and the indicated price to pay P is not greater 
than the product of e and the unit price of that 
scale. 


(W.U- P) < e.U 


4.14.3 Price Computing Instrument 


a) The price to pay shall be calculated and rounded 
to the nearest interval of price to pay, by 
multiplication of weight and unit price, both as 
indicated by the instrument. The device, which 
performs the calculations, in any case considered 
a part of the instrument. 


b 


wm 


The unit price is restricted to price/100 g or price/ 
kg. 

Not withstanding the provisions made in clause 
4.4.1, the induction of weight unit price and 
price to pay, shall remain visible after the weight 
indication is stable and after any introduction of 
the unit price, for at least one second and while the 
load is on the load receptor. 


c 


wa 


d 


Nay 


Not withstanding the provisions made in clause 
4.4.1, these indications may remain visible for not 
more than 3 s after removing the load, provided 
that the weight indication has been stable before 
and the indication would otherwise be zero. As 
long as there is a weight indication after removing 
the load, it shall not be possible to introduce or 
change a unit price. 


e 


wm 


If transaction performed by the instrument are 
printed, weight, unit price and price-to-pay shall 
all be printed. 


f) The date may be stored in a memory of the 
instrument before printing. The same data shall 
not be printed twice on the ticket for the customer. 


g) Instrument that may be used for price labeling 
purpose, must comply with 4.16 as well. 


4.14.4 Special Applications of a Price-computing 
Instrument 


a) Only if all transaction performed by the instrument 
or by connected peripheral are printed on a ticket 
or label intended for the customer, a price- 
computing instrument may perform additional 
functions, which facilitate trade and management. 
These functions shall not lead to confusion about 
the results of weighing and price computing. 


b 


eS 


Other operations or indications not covered by 
the following provisions may be performed, 
provided that no indication which could possibly 
be misunderstood as a primary indication, is 
presented to the customer. 


4.14.4.1 Non-weighed articles 


a) An instrument may accept and record positive 
or negative price to pay of one of several non- 
weighed articles, provided the weight indication 
is zero or the weighing mode is made in operative. 
The price-to pay for one or more of such articles 
shall be shown in the price-to-pay display. 


b) If the price to pay is calculated for more than 
one equal article, the number of such articles 
shall be shown on the weight display, without 
being possible taken for a weight and the price 
for one article on the unit price display unless 
supplementary display are used to show the 
number of articles and articles price. 


4.14.4.2 Totalization 


a) The instrument may totalize transaction on one or 
several tickets. The price total shall be indicated on 
the price-to-pay display and printed, accompanied 
by a special word or symbol, either at the end of the 
price-to-pay column or on a separate label ticket 
with appropriate reference to the commodities 
whose price to pay have been totalized. All prices 
to pay that are totalized shall be printed and the 
price total shall be the algebraic sum of all these 
prices as printed. 


b) An instrument may totalize transaction performed 
on other instruments linked to it, directly or 
over metrological controlled peripherals, and if 
the price-to pay scale intervals of all connected, 
instruments are identical. 


4.14.4.3 Multi-vendor operation 


An instrument may be designed to be used by more 
than one vendor or to serve more than one customer 


at the same time provided that the connection between 
the transactions and the relevant vendor or customer is 
appropriately identified. 


4.14.4.4 Cancellation 


An instrument may cancel previous transaction, where 
the transaction has already been printed relevant price- 
to-pay canceled shall be printed with an appropriate 
comment. If the transaction to the cancelled is displayed 
to the customer, it shall be clearly differentiated from 
normal transaction. 


4.14.4.5 Additional information 


An instrument may print additional information if this 
is clearly co related to the transaction and does not 
interfere with the assignment of the weight value to the 
unit symbol. 


4.14.5 Self Service Instrument 


a) A self-service instrument need not have two sets 
of scales displayed. 


b) Ifaticket or label is printed, the primary indications 
shall include a designation of the product when 
the instrument used to sell different products. 


4.15 Instruments Similar to the One Normally Used 
for Direct Sale to the Public 


An instrument similar to one normally used for direct 
sale to the public which does not comply with the 
provisions made in 4.13 and 4.14 shall carry near the 
display, the indelible marking. 


‘NOT TO BE USED FOR DIRECT SALE TO THE 
PUBLIC’ 


4.16 Price Labelling Instrument 


a) For a price-labelling instrument clause 4.14 shall 
apply; 

b) A price-labelling instrument shall have at least one 
display for the weight. It may be used temporarily 
for set-up purpose such as supervision of setting 
weight limits, unit price, pre-set tare values and 
commodity names; 


c) It shall be possible to verify, during use of the 
instruments, the actual values of unit price and 
pre-set tare value; 

d) Printing below minimum capacity shall not be 
possible; and 

e) Printing of labels with fixed values of weight, unit 
price and price-to-pay is allowed if the weighing 
mode is made in-operative. 


4.17 Mechanical Counting Instrument with Unit- 
Weight Receptor 


For the purpose of verification, a counting instrument is 
considered to be a semi-self-indicating instrument 


13 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


4.17.1 Indicating Device 


To permit verification, a counting instrument shall have 
a scale with at least one scale division d = e on either 
side of zero, the corresponding value shall be shown 
on the scale. 


4.17.2 Counting Ratio 


The counting ratio shall be shown clearly just above 
each counting platform or each counting scale mark. 


5 REQUIREMENTS FOR ELECTRONIC 
INSTRUMENTS 


In addition to 3 and 4, an electronic instrument shall 
comply with the following requirements. 


5.1 General Requirements 


5.1.1 An electronic instrument shall be designed 
and manufactured such that when it is exposed to 
disturbances either significant fault do not occur or 
significant faults are detected and acted upon. 


NOTE — A fault equal to or smaller than e is allowed 
irrespective of the value of the error of indication 


5.1.2 The requirements given in 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 and 3.9 
and at 5.1.1 shall be met durably in accordance with the 
intended use of the instrument. 


5.1.3 A pattern of an electronic instrument is presumed 
to comply with the requirements given at 5.1.1, 5.1.2 
and 5.3.2 if it passes the examinations and tests 
specified at 5.4. 


5.1.4 The requirements specified at 5.1.1 may be 
applied separately to: 


a) Each individual clause of significant fault, and 


b) Each part of the electronic instrument. 


NOTE — The choice, where clause 5.1.1 is applied, is left to 
the manufacturer. 


5.2 Acting upon Significant Faults 


When a significant fault has been detected, the 
instrument shall either be made inoperative 
automatically or a visual or audible indication shall be 
provided automatically and shall continue until such 
time as the user takes action or the fault disappears. 


5.3 Functional Requirements 


5.3.1 Upon switch-on (switch-on of indication), a special 
procedure shall be performed that shows all relevant 
signs of the indicator in the active and non-active state 
sufficiently long to be checked by the operator. 


5.3.2 An electronic instrument shall comply with the 
requirements under a relative humidity of 85 percent 
at the upper limit of the temperature range. This is not 
applicable to an electronic instrument of class I and of 
class II, if e is less than 1 g. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


5.3.3 Electronic instruments, except class I instruments, 
shall be subjected to the span stability test specified in 
clause 5.4. 


5.3.4 For the requirements given at clause 5.4 the 
error near maximum capability shall not exceed 
the maximum permissible error and the absolute 
value of the difference between the errors obtained 
for any two measurements shall not exceed half 
the verification scale interval or half the value of 
the maximum permissible error, whichever is 
greater. 


5.3.5 When an electronic instrument is subjected to 
the disturbance specified at 5.4.3, the difference 
between the weight indications without the disturbance 
(intrinsic error) shall not exceed e or the instruments 
shall detect and react to a significant fault. 


5.3.6 During the warm-up time of an electronic 
instrument there shall be no indication or transmission 
of the weighing result. 


5.3.7 An electronic instrument may be equipped 
with interfaced permitting the coupling of the 
instrument to any peripheral devices or other 
instruments. 


5.3.7.1 An interface shall not allow the metrological 
functions of the instruments measurement data to be 
inadmissible influenced by the peripheral devices 
(for example computers), by other interconnected 
instruments, or by disturbance acting on the 
interface. 


5.3.7.2 Functions that are performed or interface via 
an interface shall meet the relevant requirements and 
conditions as specified in clause 4. 

NOTE -- An “interface” comprises all mechanical, electrical 


and logic properties at the data interchange point between an 
instrument and peripheral devices or other instruments. 


5.3.7.3 It shall not be possible to introduce into an 
instrument through an interface, instructions or data 
intended or suitable to: 


a) Display data that are not clearly defined and 
could be mistaken for a weighing result or falsify 
displayed, processed or stored weighing results. 

b) Adjust the instrument or change any adjustment 

factor; however, instructions may be given through 

the interface to carry out an adjustment procedure 
using a span adjustment device incorporated 

inside the instrument or for instrument in class I, 

using an external standard mass. 

c) Falsify primary indication displayed in case direct 

sales to the public. 


5.3.7.4 An interface through which the functions 
specified at 5.3.7.3 cannot be performed or initiated 


14 


need not to be secured. Other interface shall be secured 
as per 4.1.2.4. 


5.3.7.5 An interface intended to be connected to a 
peripheral device to which the requirements of this 
clause apply, shall transmit data relating to primary 
indication in such a manner that the peripheral device 
can meet the requirements. 


5.3.7.6 A battery-operated electronic instrument shall 
continue to either function correctly or not indicate 
any weight values, wherever the voltage is below the 
manufacturer’s specified value. 


5.4 Performance and Span Stability Tests 


5.4.1 Test Considerations 


All electronic instruments of the same category, 
whether or not equipped with checking facilities, shall 
be subjected to the same performance test program. 


5.4.2 State of Instrument under Test 


5.4.2.1 Performance test shall be carried out on fully 
operational equipment in its normal operational state or 
in a status, as similar as possible thereto. 


5.4.2.2 If an electronic instrument is equipped with an 
interface permitting the coupling of the instrument to 
external equipment, the instrument shall, during the 
tests specified at A-3.1.2 to A-3.1.4 of Annex A be 
coupled to external equipment, as specified by the test 
procedure. 


5.4.3 Performance Tests 
Performance tests shall be performed according to A-2 
and A-3 of Annex A and as given Table 6. 
Table 6 Performance Tests 
( Clause 5.4.3 )

vi) Electrostatic discharge Disturbance

5.4.4 Span Stability Test 


Span stability test shall be performed according to A-4 
of Annex A. 


6 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR A 
NON-SELF INDICATING INSTRUMENTS 


A non-self-indicating instrument shall comply with the 
requirements given at 3 and 4. 


6.1 Minimum Sensitivity 


6.1.1 An extra load equivalent to the absolute value of 
the maximum permissible error for the applied load, 
shall be placed on the instrument at equilibrium and 
shall cause a permanent displacement of the indicating 
element of at least: 


a) 1 mm for an instrument of class I or II; 


b) 2 mm for an instrument of class III or IV with 
Max < 30 kg; and 


c) 5 mm for an instrument of class III or IV with 
Max > 30 kg. 


6.1.2 The sensitivity tests shall be carried out by placing 
extra loads with a slight impact in order to eliminate the 
effects of discrimination threshold. 


6.2 Indicating Device 
6.2.1 General Provisions 


6.2.1.1 Equilibrium indicating component 


If two indices are provided, with one fixed and another 
movable then the thickness of the two indicating 
components and the distance between them shall not 
exceed their thickness. However, this distance may be 
equal to 1 mm, if the thickness of the indices is less 
than this value. 


6.2.1.2 Securing 


It should be possible to secure the sliding poises, the 
removable masses and the adjusting cavities of the 
housings of such devices as per the provision of 
the Department of Weights and Measures. 


6.2.1.3 Printing 


If the device permits printing, this shall be possible only 
if sliding bars or poises or a mass switching mechanism 
are each in a position corresponding to a whole number 
of scale division. Except for accessible sliding poises or 
bars, printing shall be possible only if the equilibrium 
indicating component is in the reference position to 
within the nearest half scale interval. 


6.2.2 Sliding Poise Device 
6.2.2.1 Form of scale marks 


On bars on which the scale interval is the verification 
scale interval of the instrument, the scale marks shall 
consists of lines of constant thickness. On other 
major (or minor) bars, the scale marks shall consist of 
notches. 


15 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


6.2.2.2 Scale spacing 


The distance between scale marks shall not be less than 
2 mm and be of sufficient length so that the normal 
machining tolerance for notches or scale marks does 
not cause an error in the weighing result exceeding 0.2 
of the verification scale interval. 


6.2.2.3 Stops 


The displacement of sliding poises and minor bars shall 
be limited to the graduated part of major and minor 
bars. 


6.2.2.4 Indicating component 


Each sliding poise device shall be provided with an 
indicating component. 


6.2.2.5 Accessible sliding poise device 


a) There shall be no moving parts in sliding poises, 
except sliding minor bars. 


b) There shall be no cavity on sliding poises that 
could accidentally hold foreign bodies. 


c) It shall be possible to secure parts that are 
detachable. 


d) The displacement of sliding poises and minor bars 
shall require a certain effort. 


6.2.3 Indication by Use of Proportional Weights 


a) The reduction ratios shall be in the form 10, 
k being an integer or zero. 


b) On an instrument intended for direct sales to the 
public, the height of the raised edge of the weights 
receptor platform shall not exceed one tenth of the 
greatest dimension of the platform, without being 
more than 25 mm. 


6.3 Condition of Construction 
6.3.1 Equilibrium Indicating Component 


6.3.1.1 An instrument shall be provided with two 
moving indices or one moving indicating component 
and a fixed datum mark, the respective position of 
which indicates the reference position of equilibrium. 


6.3.1.2 On an instrument of class II or IV designed to 
be used for direct sales to the public, the indices shall 
allow the equilibrium to be seen from the opposite sides 
of the instrument. 


6.3.2 Knives, Bearings and Friction Plates 
6.3.2.1 Types of connection 
a) Levers shall be fitted with knives only and these 
shall be pivoted on bearings. 


b) The line of contact of the knives and bearing shall 
be a straight line. Counter-beams shall be pivoted 
on knife-edges. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


6.3.2.2 Knives 


a) The knives shall be fitted to the levers in such a 
way that the invariability of the ratios of the lever 
arms is assured. They shall not be welded or 
soldered. 


b) The edges of the knives of the same lever shall 
be practically parallel and shall be situated in one 
place. 


6.3.2.3 Bearings 


a) The bearings shall not be welded or soldered to 
their supports on in their mountings. 


b) It shall be possible for bearings of an instrument 
with ratio platforms and steelyards to oscillate in all 
directions on their supports or in their mountings 
on such instruments, anti-disconnection devices 
shall prevent the disconnection of articulated 
parts. 


6.3.2.4 Friction plates 


a) The longitudinal play of the knives shall be limited 
by friction plates. There shall be point contact 
between knife and friction plates and it shall be 
situated on the extension of the line(s) of contact 
between knife and bearing(s). 


b 


Nas 


The friction plate shall form a plane through the 
point of contact with the knife and its plane shall be 
perpendicular to the line of contact between knife 
and bearing. It shall not be welded or soldered to 
the bearings or their support. 


6.3.3 Hardness 

Contact parts of knives, bearings, friction plates, inter 
levers, inter lever supports and links shall have a 
hardness of at least 58 Rockwell C. 

6.3.4 Protective Coating 


A protective coating may be applied to the parts in 
contact of jointed components if this does not lead to 
changes of metrological properties. 


6.3.5 Tare Devices 

No instrument shall be fitted with a tare device. 
6.4 Simple Sliding Poise Instrument (Steelyard) 
6.4.1 General 

6.4.1.1 Scale marks 


a) The scale marks shall be lines or notches, either on 
the edge, or on the flat of the graduated shank. 


b) The minimum scale spacing shall be 2 mm 
between notches and 4 mm between lines. 


6.4.1.2 Pivots 


a) The load per unit length on the knives shall be not 
more than 10 kg/mm 


16 


b) The bores of bearing in the form of annuls shall 
have a diameter at least equal to 1.5 times the 
largest dimension of the cross section of the knife. 


6.4.1.3 Equilibrium indicating component 


The length of the equilibrium-indicating component, 
if provided taken from the edge of the fulcrum knife- 
edge of the instrument, shall be not less than 1/15 of 
the length of the graduated part of the major sliding 
poise bar. 


6.4.1.4 Distinctive mark 


The head and the sliding poise of an instrument with 
detachable sliding poises shall bear the same distinctive 
mark. 


6.4.2 Instrument with Single Capacity 


6.4.2.1 Minimum distance between knife-edges 
The minimum distance between knife-edges shall be: 


a) 25 mm for maximum capacities less than or equal 
to 30 kg; and 


b) 20 mm for maximum capacities exceeding 30 kg. 


6.4.2.2 Graduation 


The graduation shall extend from zero to the maximum 
capacity. 


6.4.2.3 Zero setting 


If an instrument of class HI or IV is provided with a 
zero-setting device, this shall be a captive screw or nut 
arrangement with a maximum effect of 4 verification 
scale intervals per revolution. 


6.5 Instrument with a Load-Measuring Device with 
Accessible Sliding Poises (of Steel Yard Type) 


6.5.1 General 


The provisions specified at 6.2 relating to load 
measuring devices with accessible sliding poises shall 
be observed. 


6.5.2 Range of Numbered Scale 


The numbered scale of the instrument shall permit 
continuous weighing from zero to the maximum 


capacity. 
6.5.3 Minimum Scale Spacing 


The scale spacing i, of the different bars (x = 1,2,3...), 
i >d le, 0.05 mm but i, > 2 mm 


6.5.4 Ratio Platform 


a) In an instrument is provided with a ratio platform 
for extending the indicating range of the numbered 
scale, the ratio between the value of the weights 
placed on the platform to balance a load and the 
load itself shall be 1/10 or 1/100. 


b) This ratio shall be indicated legibly and perman- 
ently on the beam in a position close to the ratio 
platform, in the form 1 : 10, 1 : 100 or 1/10, 1/100. 


6.5.5 Zero Setting 
An instrument shall have a zero-setting device 
consisting: 
a) Either of a cup with greatly convex cover; or 
b) Have a captive screw or nut arrangement with a 
maximum effect of 4 verification scale intervals 
per revolution. 
6.5.6 Locking of the Beam 


An instrument shall have a manual device for locking 
the beam, the action of which prevents the equilibrium 
indices coinciding when at rest. 

6.5.7 Wooden Parts 


a) Ifcertain parts of an instrument, such as the frame, 
the platform or the board are of wood, this shall be 
dry and free from defects. It shall be covered with 
paint or an effective protective varnish. 


b) No nails shall be used for the final assembly of 
wooden parts.

7.1.3.2 Dimensions 


When several plates are placed on above the other (as 
for example in the case of an instrument consisting 
of several separate devices) they shall be of the same 
width. This common width shall be fixed at 80 mm. 


7.1.3.3 Fixing 


The plate shall be fixed by rivets or screws with one 
of the rivets of red copper of material having ‘qualities 
recognized as similar. The head of one of the screws 
shall be secured by means of a lead cap inserted in a 
device that cannot be dismantled. The diameter of the 
rivet or of the lead cap shall be able to accommodate a 
stamp 4 mm in diameter. 


7.1.3.4 Dimensions of the letters 
The height of capital letter shall be at least 2 mm. 


7.1.4 Specific Cases 


7.1.4.1 Instrument having several load receptors and 
load measuring devices 


Each load measuring device which is connected or can 
be connected to one or more load receptors shall bear 
the following descriptive markings relating to these 
namely: 


a) Identification mark; 
b) Maximum capacity; 
c) Minimum capacity; 
d) Verification scale interval; and 


e) If appropriate, maximum safe load and maximum 
additive tare effect. 


7.1.4.2 Instruments consisting of separately built main 
parts 


If main parts cannot be exchanged without altering the 
metrological characteristics of the instrument, each 
unit shall have an identification mark, which shall be 
repeated in the descriptive markings. 


7.2 Verification Marks 
7.2.1 Position 


An instrument shall have a place for the application 
of verification marks. This place shall be such that 
the part of which is located cannot be removed from 
the instrument without damaging the marks, allow 
easy application of the marks without changing the 
metrological qualities of the instrument, visible without 
the instrument having to be moved, when it is in service. 


7.2.2 Mounting 


An instrument required to bear verification marks 
shall have a verification mark support, at the place 
provided for above, which ensures the conservation of 
the marks. 


18 


7.2.2.1 When the mark is of the self-adhesive type, 
a space shall be provided on the instrument for the 
application of the mark. 


8 METROLOGICAL CONTROL 


8.1 Verification 


8.1.1 Visual Inspection 


Before testing, the instrument shall be visually 
inspected for: 


a) Metrological characteristics that is, accuracy 
class, Min, Max, e and d; 


b) Prescribed inscription and position for verification 
and control marks; and 


c) Model approval number wherever applicable. 


8.1.2 Tests 


The tests shall be carried out to verify compliance with 
the following requirements; 
a) Clause 3.6.1 — Value of maximum permissible 
error; 


b) Clause 3.6.3.2 and 3.6.3.3 - Maximum permissible 
error for net and tare values; 


c) Clause 4.6.2 — Scale interval of a tare-weighing 


device; 
d) Clause 4.7.3 — Operation of the tare device shall 
be visibly indicated; 


e) Clause 3.7.1 (3 weighing on classes III and IV and 
6 weighing for I and II); 


f) Clause 3.7.2 — Eccentric loading; and 
g) Clause 3.8 — Discrimination 


8.1.3 Stamping 


Verification shall be testified by verification marks. All 
components whose dismantling or maladjustment may 
alter the metrological characteristics of the instrument 
shall be secured by a seal. 


8.2 Inspection 


a) During inspection the following tests shall be 
carried; 


b) Maximum permissible error as per clause 3.6.1; 
c) Eccentric loading as per clause 3.7.2; and 


d) The seal applied during verification shall remain 
intact. 


9 TEST PROCEDURE 
VERIFICATION AND INSPECTION 


DURING 


9.1 Evaluation of Error 


At a certain load L, the indicated value, / is noted. 
Additional weights of say 1/10 e are successively 
added until the indication of the instrument is increased 
unambiguously by one scale interval (Z + e). The 


additional load AL added to the load receptor gives the 
indication P, by using the formula, 


P-I41/2e- AL 


The error is E= P-L 
=[+1/2e—-L-—AL 


< mpe 


9.2 Weights 


9.2.1 The standard weights used for verification of an 
instrument shall not have an error greater than one third 
of the maximum permissible error of the instrument for 
the applied load. 


9.2.2 Substitution of Standard Weights 


While verifying instrument with maximum of 1 tonne 
and more, instead of standard weights, any other 
constant load may be used, provided that standard 
weights of at least 1 tonne for 50 percent of maximum, 
which is greater, shall be used. 


9.3 Weighing Tests 


9.3.1 Apply test loads from zero up to an including 
maximum and similarly remove the test loads back 
to zero. During verification 5 test loads shall be 
selected and during inspection 3 test loads shall be 
selected. 


9.3.2 The test loads selected shall include maximum, 
and values at changes. When loading or unloading, 
the weights shall be progressively increased or 
decreased. If the instrument is provided with an 
automatic zero setting devices, it shall remain in 
operation during test. Error is calculated as given 
at 9.1 above. 


9.4 Weighing Test Using Substitution Method 


9.4.1 Apply the test loads from zero up to and including 
maximum portion of the standard weights. 


9.4.2 Determine the error and then remove the weights 
so that the no-load indication, or in the case of an 
instrument with a zero tracking device, the indication 
of say 10e, is reached. 


9.4.3 Substitute the previous weights with substitution 
material until the same changeover point, as used for 
the determining of the error, is reached. Repeat the 
above procedure until maximum of the instrument is 
reached. 


9.4.4 Unload in reverse order to zero that is, unload 
the weights and determine the changeover point. Place 
the weights back and remove the substitution material 
until the same change over point is reached. Repeat this 
procedure until no-load is reached. 


19 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


9.5 Tare 


9.5.1 Tare Weighing 


Weighing tests shall be performed at least two different 
tare values. At least 5 steps may be selected including 
minimum loads close to values at which mpe changes 
and the value close to the maximum possible load (or 
maximum additive tare if provided) 


9.6 Eccentricity Test 


Large, weights shall be used in preference to several 
small weights. The load shall be applied centrally in 
the segment if several weights are used. The location 
of the load shall be marked on a sketch in the report. 
The automatic zero-setting device shall not remain in 
operation during the test. 


9.6.1 Instrument with Load Receptor having not more 
than Four Points of Supports 


The four-quarter segments roughly equal to one fourth 
of the surface of the load receptor shall be loaded 
in turn. 


9.6.2 Instruments with a Load Receptor Having more 
than Four Points of Support 


The load shall be applied over each support on an area 
of the same order of magnitude as the fraction of 1/n 
of the surface area of the load receptor, where n is the 
number of points of support. 


9.6.3 Instrument with Special Load Receptor (Tank, 
Hopper) 


The load shall be applied to each point of support. 


9.6.4 Instrument Used for Weighing Rolling Loads 


A rolling load shall be applied at different positions 
on the load receptor. These positions shall be at 
the beginning, the middle and at the end of the load 
receptor in the normal driving direction. The position 
shall be tested in the reverse direction. 


9.7 Discrimination Test 


The following tests shall be performed with three 
different loads (Min, half load and Max). 


9.7.1 Non-Self Indication and Analog Indication 


An extra load shall be placed gently on or removed from 
the load receptor while the instrument is at equilibrium. 


9.7.2 Digital Indication 


A load plus sufficient additional weights (say 10 times 
1/10 of e) shall be placed on the load receptor. The 
additional weights shall then be removed until the 
indication, / is decreased unambiguously by one actual 
scale interval that is (Z - d). One of the additional 
weights shall be replaced and a load equal to 1.4 e shall 
then be placed gently on the load receptor for and give 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


a result increased by actual scale interval above the 
initial indication, (J + d). 


9.8 Repeatability Test 


Two series of weighing shall be performed; one at half 
load and maximum. Readings shall be taken when the 
instrument is loaded and unloaded. 


9.9 Creep Test 


9.9.1 Load the instrument close to maximum. Take one 
reading as soon as the indication has stabilized and 
then note the indication while the load remains on the 
instrument for a period of four hours. During this test 
the temperature shall not very more than 2°C. 


9.9.2 The test may be terminated after 30 min if the 
indication differs less the 0.5e during the first 30 min 
and the difference between 15 and 30 min is less 
than 0.2e. 


9.10 Zero Return Tests 


9.10.1 The deviation in the zero indication before and 
after a period of loading with a load close to maximum 
for half an hour shall be determined. The reading shall 
be taken as soon as the indication has stabilized. 


9.10.2 For multiple range instruments continue to read 
the zero indication during the following 5 min after the 
indication has stabilized. 


9.10.3 If the instrument is provided with automatic zero 
setting or zero tracking, it shall not be in operation. 


9.10.4 Test for the stability of equilibrium (instruments 
with printing and/or date storage devices). 


9.10.5 Load the instrument up to 50 percent of 
maximum. Manually disturb the equilibrium and 
initiate the command for data printing or data storage 
as soon as possible. Read the indicated value 5 s after 
printing. Perform the test 5 times. 


9.11 Influence Factors 


9.11.1 Tilting 
a) The instrument shall tilt both forwards and 


backwards longitudinally, and from side to side, 
transversely. 


b 


wm 


In the text that follows, class II instrument intended 
for direct sales to the public are designated 
class II* and class II instrument not intended for 
direct sale to the public are designated class II. 


c 


S 


In practice the tests (no load and loaded) can be 

combined as follows: 

1) After zero setting in the reference position, the 
indication is determined at no load and at the 
two test loads. The instrument is then unloaded 
and tilted (without a new zero setting), after 


20 


which the indication at no load and at the two

repeated for each of the tilting directions.

In order to determine the influence of tilting on

If the instrument is provided with automatic

9.11.2 Tilting (Class IT, III and IV Instruments) 
9.11.2.1 Tilting at no-load (Class II, III and IV) 


The instrument shall be set to zero in its reference 
position (not tilted). The instrument shall then be 
tilted longitudinally up to 2/1000 or the limited value 
of the level indicator, whichever is greater. The zero 
indication is noted. The test shall be repeated with 
transverse tilting. 


9.11.2.2 Tilting when loaded (Class II, III and IV) 


The instrument shall be set to zero in its reference 
position and two weighing shall be carried out at a 
load close to the lowest load where the maximum 
permissible error changes, and at a load close to 
maximum. The instrument is then unloaded and 
tilted longitudinally and set to zero. The tilting shall 
be 2/1000 or the limiting value of the level indicator, 
whichever is greater. Weighing tests as described above 
shall be performed. The test shall be repeated with 
transverse tilting. 


9.11.2.3 Tilting class I instrument 


a) The instrument shall be tilted longitudinally up to 
the limiting value of the level indicator. Check the 
tilt. Repeat with transverse tilting. 


b) If the tilt is not greater than 2/1000, no further 
testing is required otherwise test as per 9.11.2.2 
above. 


9.11.2.4 Instrument without level indicator 


For an instrument liable to tilted and not fitted with a 
level indicator the test specified at 9.11.2.1 and 9.11.2.2 
shall be performed except that the instrument shall be 
tilted 5 percent instead of 0.2 percent. 


9.12 Warm up Time Test 


a) An instrument using electric power shall be 
disconnected from the supply for a period of at 
least 8 h prior to the test. The instrument shall 
then be connected and switched on and as soon 
as the indication has stabilized, the instrument 
shall be set to zero and the error at zero shall be 
determined. Calculation of error shall be made. 
The instrument shall be loaded with a load close 


b) 


9.13 


to maximum. These observations shall be repeated 
after 5, 15 and 30 min. 

For instruments of class I, the provisions of 
the operating manual for the time following 
connection to the mains shall be observed.

9.13.1 Static Temperature Tests 

a) The test consists of exposure of the equipment 
under test (EUT) to constant (*) temperatures 
within the range stated under free air conditions, 
for a 2 h period after the EUT has reached 
temperature stability. 

b) The weighing tests (loading and unloading) shall 
be carried out: 

1) Atareference temperature (normally 20°C but 
for class I instruments the mean value of the 
specified temperature limits); 

2) At the specified high temperature; 

3) At the specified low temperature; 

4) At a temperature of 5°C if the specified low 
temperature is below 10°; and 

5) At the reference temperature. 

c) The change of temperature shall not exceed 1°C/ 
min during heating and cooling down.

The instrument shall be set to zero and then

period after the instrument has reached stability at 
this temperature.
