9.14 Voltage Variation 


9.14.1 Stabilize the equipment under test (EUT) under 
constant environmental conditions. 


9.14.2 The test consists of subjecting the equipment 
under test (EUT) to variations of ac mains voltage. 


9.14.3 The test shall be performed with test loads of 
10e and a load between half of the maximum and 
maximum. 


9.14.4 Test Severity — Voltage Variations 
a) Upper limit: V +10 percent, and 


b) Lower limit: V -15 percent. 


Where, V is the value of voltage marked on the 
instrument. 


9.14.5 Maximum Allowable Variations 


a) All functions shall operate as designed; 


b) All indications shall be within the maximum 
permissible errors; and 

c) If the instrument is provided with an automatic 
zero-setting or a zero tracking device, it may be in 
operation during the test. 


22 


9.15 Endurance Test 


NOTE — Applicable only to instruments of class II, III and IV 
with Max < 100 kg 


9.15.1 The endurance test shall be performed after all 
other tests. 


9.15.2 Under normal conditions of use, the instrument 
shall be subjected to the repetitive loading and 
unloading of a load approximately equal to 50 percent 
of maximum. The load shall be applied 1 00 000 times. 
The frequency and speed of application shall be such 
that the instrument attains equilibrium when loaded 
and when unloaded. The force of the load applied 
shall not exceed the force attained in a normal loading 
operation. 


9.15.3 A weighing test in accordance with the 
procedure shall be performed before the endurance 
test is started to obtain the intrinsic error. A weighing 
test shall be performed after the completion of the 
loadings to determine the durability error due to wear 
and tear. 


9.15.4 If the instrument is provided with automatic 
zero-setting or zero-tracking device it may be in 
operation during the test. 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


ANNEX A 
( Clause 3.10 and 5.4) 


ADDITIONAL TESTS FOR ELECTRONIC INSTRUMENTS 


FOR MODEL APPROVAL 
A-1 GENERAL REQUIREMENT FOR A-3 POWER VOLTAGE VARIATIONS 
ELECTRONIC INSTRUMENTS UNDER 
TEST (EUT) A-3.1 Performance Tests for Disturbances 


A-1.1 Energize the EUT for a time equal to or greater 
than the warm up time specified by the manufacturer 
and maintain the EUT energized for the duration of 
the test. 


A-1.2 Adjust the EUT as closely as practicable to zero 
prior to each test, and do not re-adjust it at any time 
during the test, except to reset it if a significant fault has 
been indicated. The deviation of the no-load indication 
due to any test condition shall be recorded, and any 
load indication shall be corrected accordingly to obtain 
the weighing result. 


A-1.3 The handling of the instrument shall be such 
that no condensation of water occurs on the 
instrument.

FACTORS 


A-2.1 Static Temperatures

instruments where e is less than 1 g).

a) The test consists of exposure of the EUT to 
a constant temperature and constant relative 
humidity. The EUT shall be tested with at least 
five different test loads.

A-3.1.1 Short Time Power Reductions 
A-3.1.1.1 Test procedure in brief 


a) Stabilize the EUT under constant environmental 
conditions; 


b) A test generator capable of reducing the amplitude 
of one or more half cycles (at zero crossings) or the 
AC mains voltage shall be used. The test generator 
shall be adjusted before connecting the EUT. The 
mains voltage reduction shall be repeated ten 
times with an interval of at least 10 s. 

The test shall be performed with test loads of 
10e and a load between half of the maximum and 
maximum.

A-3.1.2 Burst 

The test consists in exposing the EUT to specified 
bursts of voltage spikes. 

A-3.1.2.1 Test procedure in brief 


a) Before any test stabilize the EUT under constant 
environmental conditions, the test shall be applied 
separately to: 

1) Power supply lines, and 

2) T/O circuits and communications lines, if any. 
The test shall be performed with test loads of 
10e and a load between half of the maximum and 
maximum.

A-3.1.3 Electrostatic Discharge 


A-3.1.3.1 Test procedure in brief 


a) The test consists in exposing the EUT to specified, 
direct and indirect, electrostatic discharges. 


b) The test includes the paint penetration method, if 
appropriate, for direct discharges the air discharge 
shall be used where the contact discharge method 
cannot be applied; 


Before any test stabilizes the EUT under constant 
environmental conditions, at least 10 direct 
discharges and 10 indirect discharges shall be 
applied. The time interval between successive 
discharges shall be at least 10 s; 


The test shall be performed with test loads of 
10e and a load between half of the maximum and 
maximum; and 


c 


wm 


d 


Nay 


e) Maximum allowable variations. 


The difference between the weight indications due 
to the disturbance and the indication without the 
disturbance shall either not exceed e or the instrument 
shall detect and react to a significant fault. 


A-3.1.4 Immunity to Radiated Electromagnetic Fields 


A-3.1.4.1 Test procedure in brief 

a) The test consists in exposing the EUT to specified 
electromagnetic fields. 

b) Before any test, stabilize the EUT under constant 
environmental conditions, the EUT shall be 
exposed to electromagnetic fields of the strength 
and character as specified by the severity level. 


c) The test shall be performed with one small test 


load only: 
1) Frequency range 26 — 1 000 MHz 
2) Field strength 3 V/m 
3) Modulation 80 percent AM, 1 kHz 
sine wave 


d) Maximum allowable variations — The difference 
betweenthe weightindication due tothe disturbance 
and the indication without the disturbance shall 
either not exceed e or the instrument shall detect 
and react to a significant fault. 


A-4 SPAN STABILITY TEST 
(Not applicable to class I instruments) 


A-4.1 Test Procedure in Brief 


a) The test consists in observing the variations of 
the error of the EUT under sufficiently constant 


24 


3 


ambient conditions (reasonably constant 
conditions in a normal laboratory environment) at 
various intervals before, during and after the EUT 
has been subjected to performance tests. 


b 


wm 


The performance test shall include the temperature 
test and if applicable, the damp heat test; they shall 
not include any endurance test; other performance 
test in this annexure and given at 9 shall be 
performed. 


The EUT shall be disconnected from the mains 
power supply, or battery supply where fitted, two- 
time for at least 8 h during the period of the test. 
The number of disconnections may be increased if 
the manufacturer specified so or at the discretion 
of the approval authority in the absence of any 
such specification. 


c 


wm 


d) The manufacturer’s operating instructions shall be 
considered for the conduct of this test. 


e) The EUT shall be stabilized at sufficiently constant 
ambient conditions after switch-on for at least five 
hours, but at least 16 h after the temperature and 
damp heat test have been performed. 


f) Test duration shall be 28 days or the period 
necessary for the performance tests to be carried 
out, whichever is shorter. 


g) Time between measurements — between half 
and 10 days. 


h) Test load — Near Max: The same test weights 
shall be used throughout this test. 


j) Number of measurement shall be at least 8. 
k) Test sequence: 


1) Stabilize all factors at sufficiently constant 
ambient conditions. 


2) Adjust the EUT as close to zero as possible. 


3) Automatic zero tracking shall be made 
inoperative and automatic built in span 
adjustment device shall be made operative. 


4) Apply the test weight(s) and determine the 
error. 


5) At the first measurement immediately repeat 
zeroing and loading four times to determine 
the average value of the error. For the next 
measurements perform only one unless the 
result is outside either the specified tolerance 
or the range of the five readings of the initial 
measurements is more than 0.le. 


Record the following data: 
1) Data and time, 

2) Temperature, 

3) Barometric pressure, 
4) Relative humidity, 

5) Test load, 

6) Indication, 


7) Errors, and 
8) Changes in test locations. 


n) Apply all necessary corrections resulting from 
variations of temperature, pressure, etc. between 
the various measurements. 


p) Allow full recovery of the EUT before any other 
test is performed. 


q) Maximum allowable variations: 


1) The variation in the errors of indication shall 
not exceed half the verification scale interval 
or half the absolute value of the maximum 
permissible error on initial verification or the 


25 


IS 16514 (Part 2) : 2019 


test load applied, whichever in greater, on any 
of the measurements. 


2) Where the difference of the results indicate a 
trend more than half the allowable variation 
specified above, the test shall be continued 
until the trend comes to rest or reverses 
itself, or until the error exceeds the maximum 
allowable variation. 

NOTE -- Weighing instruments in use as per the specification 

prevailing immediately before the coming into force of 

the present Heading B (of the Seventh Schedule of Legal 

Metrology General Rules, 2011) shall continue to be used in 

any transaction or for industrial production, so long as such 

instruments lasts. 


Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
